tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit, branch, push, or stash; leave changes uncommitted. Do not call any MCP tool or App and do not capture anything to an external system.

HOW YOU WILL BE GRADED, stated up front so you are not guessing. A checker runs after you and it will FAIL you for any of these:
- changing a file outside your owned list (below);
- changing production code and adding no tests at all;
- adding fewer than 4 new `def test_...` functions;
- adding no NEGATIVE test, meaning nothing in your diff uses pytest.raises, asserts a blocked or failed result, or otherwise proves a guard stops bad input;
- the test suite not passing.
There is no document or summary format requirement. Write whatever notes you like, or none.

YOUR OWNED FILES, the only paths you may touch:
  server/pipeline/interview_transcription.py
  tests/test_interview_transcription.py
  tests/test_interview_transcription_grid.py

BACKGROUND. This repo produces a two-person video podcast. Every episode begins as four separate WebM files from a Daily.co room: host camera audio, host camera video, guest camera audio, guest camera video. They do not share a zero. Tracks also contain dropouts, meaning stretches where packets stopped arriving.

A module already exists and is correct: server/pipeline/av_sync.py derive_timeline() computes ONE session grid with T=0 at the earliest packet across all four tracks and records every dropout as a hole; build_stems() renders four stems that are all exactly the same length on that grid, HOLDING each dropout as silence rather than deleting it. It writes timeline.json describing the grid, each track's grid offset, and every hole.

THE DEFECT YOU ARE FIXING, measured on a real episode and not hypothetical. interview_transcription.py builds its own zero by parsing a 13-digit epoch out of each source filename (near lines 314 and 352) and adding that flat offset to the speech engine's local times (near lines 439 and 455). It has NO model of dropouts. On the reference episode the host's raw audio decodes to 2765.311s because its 76.86-second hole collapses during decode, so every host timestamp after 151.859s is up to 76.86 SECONDS early.

The measured proof: the session is 2842.196s long. The host's last transcript segment ends at 2761.45s, which is 80.7s short. Seven host segments are timestamped INSIDE the 151.859 to 228.719 hole window, which is impossible in real time. The guest's track has no holes, so the guest's timestamps are correct and end at 2840.77s. One transcript file, two different time bases, and nothing in the code knows. Downstream, clips are cut using these numbers, so a clip chosen for something the host said lands more than a minute from him saying it.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. A mode that transcribes the STEMS instead of the raw tracks. Stems are hole-filled and all four are exactly the same length on one grid, so the speech engine's local times ARE grid times: apply the grid origin and nothing else. No filename parsing, no per-track guessing, no flat epoch offset.

2. A plausibility guard that makes the old failure detectable rather than silent. After producing timestamps for a track, compare that track's last timestamp against the known session length, and flag or fail a track whose transcript ends implausibly early. Make the tolerance a named constant with a comment explaining that an 80-second shortfall against a 2842-second session is what this exists to catch. This single check would have caught the entire defect.

3. Close the silent-zero path. Today, if a filename does not match the expected pattern, that track's offset silently stays 0.0 and the transcript is quietly wrong. In the new mode that must be impossible; make it raise or fail rather than default.

ADDITIVE ONLY. The existing filename-offset path and every current caller must behave exactly as they do today. A later step wires the orchestrator to switch the new mode on. If you change current default behavior the suite goes red and the work cannot integrate. Additive means a new keyword argument defaulting to old behavior, or a new function beside the old one. Never remove the old path.

TESTS ARE THE DELIVERABLE AS MUCH AS THE CODE. At minimum prove: the stems mode produces timestamps on the grid; the plausibility guard FIRES on a track that ends 80 seconds early (use the real numbers above as the fixture); the guard does NOT fire on a healthy track; and the unmatched-filename case raises instead of silently defaulting to zero. You may mock the speech engine; do not require real audio.
tasks.verified: stems-mode transcription with a plausibility guard, at least 4 new tests including a negative case, suite green, current behavior unchanged
